title: Progress of Nation-wide COVID-19 Vaccination Programme
what_it_is: Progress of Nation-wide COVID-19 Vaccination Programme

sections.label: COVID-19 vaccination programme questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Health about vaccination progress, side effects, vaccination sites, vaccine orders, delivery schedules and centre capacity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the progress of the COVID-19 vaccination programme since it was launched; (b) among those who took the vaccination so far, how many have suffered side effects; (c) where will the vaccination sites be located for the wider population; and (d) whether the accessibility of these sites will be considered, particularly for the elderly and those with mobility problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) to date, what is the progress of the national COVID-19 vaccination programme; (b) what are the types of side effects observed; and (c) how many instances of severe side effects are there requiring emergency care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Government can provide an update as to how the COVID-19 vaccination programme is progressing especially with regard to any adverse reactions to the vaccinations so far and how such cases, if any, have been managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what are the numbers and kinds of COVID-19 vaccines that Singapore has ordered and what are their delivery schedules; (b) how many vaccination centres will be set up in the next six months and what is the capacity of the vaccination centres; and (c) how many people have received the COVID-19 vaccination as of end-January 2021 and how many of them have shown symptoms of side effects, if any.

sections.label: Vaccine safety standards
sections.summary: Only vaccines meeting strict standards of safety, quality and effectiveness will be used for the population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Only vaccines that meet strict standards of safety, quality and effectiveness will be used for our population.

sections.label: First dose vaccinations by 31 January
sections.summary: As of 31 January 2021, more than 155,000 individuals had received their first dose of the vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As of 31 January 2021, yesterday, more than 155,000 individuals have received their first dose of the vaccine.

sections.label: Around 40 vaccination centres planned
sections.summary: About 40 vaccination centres are planned, each with an estimated capacity of about 2,000 vaccinations per day on average.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In total, we are planning to set up around 40 vaccination centres, with each vaccination centre planned for an estimated capacity of about 2,000 vaccinations per day on average.

sections.label: Polyclinics begin COVID-19 vaccinations
sections.summary: From 1 February 2021, all 20 polyclinics across Singapore will begin offering COVID-19 vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: From 1 February 2021, today, all 20 polyclinics across Singapore will also begin offering COVID-19 vaccinations.

sections.label: Local anaphylaxis incidence rate
sections.summary: The local incidence rate of anaphylaxis is about 2.6 per 100,000 doses administered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The incidence rate of anaphylaxis locally is about 2.6 per 100,000 doses administered.

sections.label: COVID-19 vaccination roll-out and prioritisation
sections.summary: Singapore has advance purchase agreements with Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna and Sinovac, and prioritises healthcare and frontline workers while targeting vaccination of all residents by end-2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We seek everyone's patience and support, as we progressively roll out the vaccinations to the whole population in tandem with the shipments of the vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have signed advance purchase agreements with Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna and Sinovac, and are in discussions with a few other pharmaceutical companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: While there will be some delay to the shipments of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine due to the upgrading of Pfizer's manufacturing plant, we will continue to monitor our supplies closely to meet our target of vaccinating all Singaporeans and long-term residents in Singapore by the end of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Given the present, short-term limited supply of COVID-19 vaccines globally, there is a need to prioritise the vaccinations at this point in time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have prioritised healthcare workers and COVID-19 frontline personnel whose work requires them to be in constant contact with individuals who may be infected.

sections.label: Vaccine vial doses and wastage
sections.summary: A vial is supplied with around five doses, but more than five doses are on average obtained per vial, keeping wastage rates low.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Yes, Sir, I will just stop at that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I do not have the specific number at this point in time, but in general, a vial is supplied to have around five doses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Because of the way the manufacturer does this, usually there is a bit more inside the vial.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And I can tell you on average we are getting more than five doses per vial because of the way in which we have centrally controlled the thawing distribution as well as the training for the people who do the vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, our wastage rates are low and well-managed.

sections.label: Early vaccination for grassroots volunteers
sections.summary: A suggestion for early vaccination of grassroots leaders and volunteers is well taken, and almost all documented adverse events have onset close to vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The suggestion about early vaccinations for grassroots leaders and other volunteers going out to convince seniors or to help seniors make the appointment, is well taken.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It may not be possible to ensure that everybody has a vaccination at that point in time, but perhaps we can go at least to the point of ensuring they have a booking and then when you are facing the senior, you can say, "Well, I have not got it yet, but here is my appointment and I know that I am going to get it because I have committed to doing so." For the adverse event reporting, I would point out that almost all adverse events documented from vaccinations, tend to have an onset very close to the administration of the vaccination.

sections.label: Whole-of-Government vaccination communications approach
sections.summary: MOH and other Government agencies are coordinating communications material in various languages, levels of detail and channels.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MOH, together with all the different Government agencies involved are coordinating a whole-of-Government communications approach.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will produce material in a variety of languages, we will produce material for different levels of interests – the top line messages all the way down to the detailed advisories for the healthcare practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And we will distribute this across a variety of channels – letters, online, mainstream media, broadcast media.

sections.label: Confusion over vaccination advice
sections.summary: There is some confusion over advice and questions about other safety issues, but there are no plans to change vaccination roll-out targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, there is some confusion over this advice and they are wondering if there is any other safety issues that they should consider before proceeding to vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There are no plans to change our targets for vaccination roll-out.

sections.label: Breastfeeding mothers and vaccination
sections.summary: It depends on the individual mother's case, but there is no absolute contraindication for a breastfeeding mother to proceed with vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It depends on the specific individual case of the mother.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But if I could sum up the position and explain some of the reasons for the confusion, there is no absolute contraindication for a breastfeeding mother to proceed with vaccination.

sections.label: Early vaccination waitlist request
sections.summary: The Ministry will open registration and seek indication of interest from eligible members of the public for this phase and the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider a waitlist for those who want to go for early vaccination, especially if there are strong reasons for them to go overseas, be it for health, studies, business or on compassionate grounds?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will be opening up the registration process and we will be looking for an indication of interest from members of the public who are eligible in this phase as well as in the future.

sections.label: Vaccination capacity by third quarter
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification and states Singapore has the capacity and capability to vaccinate its population by the third quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like a clarification on that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We certainly have the capacity and the capability to vaccinate our population by the third quarter of this year.

sections.label: Vaccination timeline and outcome factors
sections.summary: The aim is between the end of the third quarter and the end of the year, determined by supply and Singaporeans' willingness to be vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Over the next few months, we can also anticipate that further information will be available from the vaccination process that is happening around the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, there is a band that we are aiming for somewhere between the end of the third quarter and the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Ultimately, the outcome will be determined by a combination of our supply as well as the willingness and the engagement of Singaporeans and long-term residents to go forward to have the vaccination.
